messages:
nina: I opened PR https://git.redwood/workspace/docs/pull/867 to update the Hephaestus-4b model card. Quick summary of issues I found: Python snippet uses old streaming API, limits table lists max_input_tokens=8192 but our perf run stabilizes to ~6,500, an external micro-bench link 404s, and there's no guidance on dynamic batching for multi-request scenarios. Can folks take bits?
oscar: I'll take the Python snippet swap to SDK v3 patterns. Which streaming pattern do we want? for-await-of or context manager?
nina: Prefer for-await-of for brevity and also include a tiny sync example. Also add a small note showing how to enable prefix caching in code.
desired snippet: show `from redwood import Client` + streaming for-await-of.
liam: I'll validate bench data. Path is s3://redwood-bench/hephaestus-4b/2026-02/perf.csv. The GPU mem curve shows degradation after ~6.5k tokens; upstream model metadata lists 8,192. We should be explicit: tested max 6,500; catalog ceiling 8,192.
yasmin: I'll prepare copy for the limits table and an explanatory footnote: "tested max (tokens): 6,500; catalog ceiling: 8,192 (upstream ceiling, not validated by Redwood). For reproducibility see s3 path." Also add a short compatibility bullet about quant variants and runtime support.
oscar: Draft streaming snippet pushed: ```python
from redwood import Client
client = Client()
stream = await client.text.stream(model="hephaestus-4b")
await stream.send("Summarize the following:")
for await (const chunk of stream):
    print(chunk.delta, end="")
```
(Will adapt to Python async/await syntax properly in PR)
liam: Replaced broken micro-bench link with bench index and added s3 path in the card: https://bench.redwood/internal/index + s3://redwood-bench/hephaestus-4b/2026-02/. Note in PR that the index is internal-only.
yasmin: For dynamic batching guidance I'll add a short example: combine small requests into batch of N where N*avg_tokens <= GPU_mem_budget, use per-model recommended batch sizes (e.g., 8-16 for hephaestus-4b), and show pseudo-code for a batching queue. Also mention tradeoffs: higher batch -> lower p99 latency but better throughput.
nina: Good. Another micro: benchmarks section lists "throughput: 4.2k tok/s @4k"  can we make it explicit whether that's end-to-end or token-stream throughput? We should label as "steady-state token throughput" if it's per-token.
ioscar: I'll adjust copy to "steady-state token throughput (measured at 4k)".
pr-bot: preview-build: https://staging.docs.redwood/pr-867  preview will update on commits.
nina: One more: supported-variants table missing `hephaestus-4b-optim` (lower memory, different quant). Add with note: "optim: lower mem, reduced tested max (4,000 tokens)".
yasmin: Added the variant entry and included a compatibility note: "optim uses q4f16 and is recommended on Dedicated/Private; hosted uses q4a for latency-sensitive requests."\liam: Quick QA checklist in PR desc: smoke test snippets with @redwood/sdk@3.6.x, confirm staging renders, check bench link for internal access, and verify the limits footnote s3 path.
nina: Thank you everyone  will request review once oscar's snippet has correct async-python syntax and liam confirms bench path. Aim to merge tomorrow if no blockers.
